以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
CGC_OA_ASYNC was compared with `!= nullptr` at ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:1745, and scripts/run_server.sh puts CGC_OA_ASYNC into the server env unconditionally, so there was no value -- not "0", not "" -- that selected the non-segmented path. The A/B pair built to test whether the segment ordering causes the S1 divergence therefore re-ran the segmented arms exactly: md5 sets {dc055e63} and {29ca694a, 672585db, b8c705cc}, pool counters misses 13040 / 14296 and file_reads 36360 / 39948, all digit-for-digit identical to the segmented run. The near-miss is the expensive part: the pair looks like a clean refutation of the ordering hypothesis and would have closed a live hypothesis on the strength of an experiment that changed no variable. This is the mirror image of the run_server.sh allowlist trap (an unlisted variable is silently DROPPED, so 'no effect' and 'not set' are indistinguishable); here the variable IS set and its value is IGNORED, so 'no effect' and 'the switch is not wired' are indistinguishable. The positive discipline that follows: a null result from a switch is evidence only once the switch has been shown to change something, and reading the consumer is the cheapest such demonstration -- cheaper than the run it is meant to justify.

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
eng-20260915-213356-p25-slotgpu-noasync-r1

它管轄的檔案：`src/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp`, `scripts/run_server.sh`

Before recording a switch's null result as a refutation, read the branch condition that consumes it: an env var tested with `getenv(...) != nullptr` selects on PRESENCE, so setting it to "0" (or to an empty string) takes the same branch as "1".

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
SONAME 內嵌 commit 數（libllama-common.0.0.<N>.dylib），所以每次全量重建都會換檔名，舊檔留在原地變成孤兒；而載入器走的是 symlink 鏈（libllama-common.dylib → libllama-common.0.dylib → libllama-common.0.0.275.dylib，用 otool -L 可確認）。重測腳本的證據頭把檔名寫死成 0.0.239，於是兩份報告都印「MTP_SUPPORT 字串 ABSENT」——與事實相反：兩次崩潰報告的 usedImages 都顯示實際載入的是 libllama-common.0.0.275.dylib（UUID 4ddc4e5d-ebb1-39e6-9e6a-1819404f1be3，3/3 受 guard 字串俱在）。錯誤方向剛好是「開關沒開」，會把整條 MTP 觀測鏈引到另一條路上（連帶讓「MTP_SUPPORT 有沒有編與崩潰的關係」這種問題問錯）。另一件事同時成立：增量 cmake --build 只重編 CMake 自己判定為 stale 的 TU（本輪 411 個 .o 全部最新、只重編了 test-quantize-stats.cpp.o），所以「libllama-common 的 .o 是 09-14、speculative.cpp 是 09-13」這種 mtime 比較可以同時成立於一個完全一致的 build；那個 build dir 的一致性要靠 flags.make 的內容比對，不是 mtime。修正後改為從 otool -L 反推 10 個載入 artifact 並逐一 realpath，輸出判準句 guarded 3/3 + control present => MTP_SUPPORT=ON (compiled in)。

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
第一次的正對照就測錯檔：拿 libllama-common.0.0.239.dylib（tracked、重建時沒有被覆寫）做 before/after，得到雜湊相同而得不出結論；改測重建產生的 0.0.275 才得到 0/3 → 3/3。另一面：run_server.sh:325-341 新增的 MTP 可見性守門兩面都量過——好 build 0 warning、舊 dylib 標記數 0（會 warning）、現行 3（不 warning）；control 字串缺失代表 artifact 壞掉，不是開關沒開，所以判準句必須把 control 一起印出來。順帶更正：這份寫死的證據頭不只「修後」那一份錯，修前那一份也錯（它當時就宣稱 MTP 沒編，而事實是已經編了）。 同族的第二個實例（2026-09-16 實測）：閘門的檔案比對樣式漏一種副檔名，等於對那個類別完全無效。scripts/check_build_tracked.sh 的檢查 8 用一個 case 樣式挑出「會被編進 binary 的 llama 原始碼」，原本列了 *src/*.cpp|*.h|*.c|*.mm|*.metal，獨漏 .m（只列了 Objective-C++ 的 .mm）。後果：改 ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-context.m 會被判成「8 無 llama 原始碼變更（僅 doc/腳本/產物）」，一個假 PASS，而且它同時跳掉了「產物有沒有一起 staged」與「binary 是否比原始碼新」兩條。已補上 *src/*.m（該 repo 只有 2 個 .m，都在 ggml/src/ggml-metal/，都編進 libggml-metal，所以樣式是精確的）；陽性對照：餵一份含 .m 的假 staged 清單，staged_src 由 0 → 1，檢查 8 隨即改印 「build 產物隨原始碼 staged」+「binary 比 staged 原始碼新（已重建）」。

它管轄的檔案：`Backup/run_req2_retest.sh`, `scripts/run_server.sh`, `scripts/check_build_tracked.sh`, `agent_harness/CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/PREFILL250_THERMAL_TRANSIENT_20260916.html`
稽核編譯期開關時，要量「載入器實際映射的那個檔案」的字串存在性——從 otool -L 反推 @rpath 載入集再逐一 realpath——並同時印出不受 guard 保護的 control 字串。不要把檔名寫死，也不要用 mtime 當一致性證據。

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
2026-09-16：以 notify key 為閘門時，直覺會要求 Level 全程為 0。實測否證：15:18:46 那一臂發射時 0/NOMINAL，外掛 2 Hz 探針顯示 15:19:13 升 1、15:19:24 升 2（皆在臂中途），而該臂三個請求仍是 257.41/253.42/262.64，全部 ≥250。15:31:04 那一臂則全程 0/NOMINAL（after req3 才翻 1），讀數 266.81/269.35/271.64。所以閘門讀『發射前那一刻』：發射 0 → 6/6 ≥250（最低 253.42）；發射 1 或 2 → 0/21 ≥250（最高 211.65）。落後的原因（governor 對熱壓訊號反應有延遲）是假設，HTTP 路徑上沒有 per-request 的 DVFS 證據，所以不寫成機制結論。

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
Backup/cgc_logs/thermal_gate/req2retest_20260916_151846.txt（中途升 1→2，仍全部 ≥250）vs Backup/cgc_logs/thermal_gate2/req2retest_20260916_153104.txt（全程 0，全部 ≥250）

它管轄的檔案：`Backup/run_thermal_gate.sh`, `Backup/run_req2_retest.sh`, `docs/PREFILL250_CONDITIONAL_DELIVERY_20260916.html`
一個條件要在**哪一刻**讀，本身是條件的一部分，必須由資料決定而不是由直覺決定。若某個讀數在事件中途會改變，就要問「改變之後那個事件有沒有被撤回」；如果沒有，閘門讀的是事件開始前那一刻，而不是要求全程成立。而且閘門的讀數與它要授權的數字要**同時同地**取得（in-band），不能事後重建——否則條件的時間戳與數字的時間戳無法對齊。

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
`CGC-DECPROF` 會印 `top8:` 與（開 `_ALL` 時）`all:`，描述的是同一批層。第一版 harvester 把兩種都 append，於是一個 40 層的模型報成 `layers_seen=48`（40+8）。這不只是計數錯誤：它把重複層塞進 `max` 與變異數，而「該層是均勻變慢還是單層問題」正是用 `max/mean` 與 CV 判的——同一份資料因此被判成 LOCALISED，真值是 UNIFORM。改成以層號為鍵的 dict 之後 `layers_seen=40`，中位數/IQR 也才可信。

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
sweep 第一個 session 的 run 1 被印成 `layer wait over 48 layers: ... peak/mean=1.667 -> LOCALISED`；同一個圖改用去重後的穩健統計是 `median=363.13 ms, IQR/median=0.094`，即 uniform。

它管轄的檔案：`scripts/check/prefill_certifiability.py`, `scripts/check/prefill_idle_sweep.py`
當一個儀器同時輸出「全部」與「前 N 名」兩種視圖時，harvester 必須按**實體鍵**去重，不能把兩種行都 append 進一個 list——前 N 名是全部的子集，兩者相加等於把那些實體數了兩次。

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
Running the pool-row capture at depth 12 (needed because a 2-token chunk has 16 ids and the anomaly sits at the second token) produced 4 rows of sentinel on every single-token graph, because a decode step's operand holds only 8 ids. The comparator flagged 15 of 105 keys as PART-READ -- three of the three node names on each of the five decode graphs -- and a PART-READ key has no verdict, so the first A/B of the new instrument appeared to be missing a fifth of its evidence. The capture already printed the operand size (`nsel`), which is what makes min(depth, nsel) the correct row count rather than a guess.

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
Run 2026-09-17 11:1x: `verdict rows: SAME=90 DIFF=0 PART-READ=15 NOT-READ=0` before the fix, with `causes: UNCLASSIFIED-SAME-ID=1200 UNREAD=60`; after bounding the row count by `nsel` the same pair of logs gives `SAME=105 DIFF=0 PART-READ=0 NOT-READ=0` and `causes: SAME=1200`. The per-graph decomposition then shows the decode graphs with exactly 8 compared rows and the prompt chunks with 12, which is what the operands actually hold.

它管轄的檔案：`Backup/compare_pool_row.py`

The number of rows a comparator may compare is bounded by the OPERAND's size on both sides, not by the depth the capture was ASKED for. A capture that digests 'the first N ids the consumer used' writes fewer rows than N whenever the operand holds fewer ids, and the unwritten rows are pure sentinel -- so a comparison that iterates to N manufactures a 'measurement gap' verdict for a region that never existed. Distinguish three things that all look like a short reading: rows BEYOND the operand (exclude; not part of the question), rows the operand has but the reader did not cover (report as a gap, with the covered prefix named), and rows covered but never written (a genuine instrumentation failure). Record the operand's size in the row so the reader can tell them apart -- a capture depth that is a knob cannot double as the operand's size.

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
`CGC-SEG` 印的是 `w_us/n`（累積平均，數值會隨 n 上升而下降）。第一版 harvester 把 13 行印出來的平均值全部加起來，得到 0.54 s；同一批 log 的正確總量是 30.66 s（差 57×）。錯誤值的方向是『讓等待看起來不存在』，正好會把 GPU 瓶頸誤判成沒有瓶頸。

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
prefill_certifiability.py 的 harvest_segments 第一版：seg_wait_us=544570 （把累積平均加總），實際 seg_wait_s=30.66。

它管轄的檔案：`scripts/check/prefill_certifiability.py`, `agent_harness/CONVENTIONS.md`
對『累積平均』型態的儀器輸出，只能取最後一行 × 它的 n；逐行加總沒有意義。

以下是引擎調校迴圈此刻的狀態。決定**下一個該做什麼**：一個具體的動作，
不要複述狀態。已經被排除的路線不要再走一次。

QUESTION: With the ids proven bit-identical, does repairing the pool/slot content (a) make D3 admissible and (b) deliver the 16.82 t/s that the submit-ahead probe measured -- without the probe's race?

EVIDENCE ON HAND:
- [artifact docs/REMAP_ROUNDTRIP_REMOVAL_PLAN_2026-09-15.md (§9.18.3)] Per (graph, node) pairing against the baseline arm: graphs 0/1/2 are 117/117 bit-identical; graphs 3/4 are 3 SAME / 114 DIFF. The surviving 3 are layer 1's gate/up/down. So the captured ids, and the table lookup that produced them, are proven identical on shared input.
- [artifact docs/REMAP_ROUNDTRIP_REMOVAL_PLAN_2026-09-15.md (§9.18.4)] Layer 1's router ids are identical => its input and router logits are identical; layer 1's MoE ids are identical; yet layer 2's router differs. Same input + same ids + different output => the defect is in the weight content the ids point at, i.e. the pool/slot contents, not in ids and not in the mapping function.
- [artifact docs/REMAP_ROUNDTRIP_REMOVAL_PLAN_2026-09-15.md (§9.17d)] D3's premise is that the graph no longer contains a per-step host write. But the slot_table that slot_lookup reads is still a host-written tensor (publish_slot_table), so the real condition is 'publication is not on the hot path'. Explicitly marked UNTESTED.
- [artifact docs/REMAP_ROUNDTRIP_REMOVAL_PLAN_2026-09-15.md (§1-§2, the D0 probe)] CGC_SUBMIT_AHEAD=1 lifts llama-bench decode 9.16/9.45 -> 16.82 t/s (x1.78), step 82.5 -> 31-44 ms, and ~44% of step time is pipeline-removable. The output is deliberately corrupt; it is a ceiling probe, never a candidate.
- [artifact docs/REMAP_ROUNDTRIP_REMOVAL_PLAN_2026-09-15.md (§9.17b, §9.17g)] Under D3 the probe's number changes meaning: from 'the S2 ceiling' to 'the total value of the segment boundary (= the S3 ceiling)'. And §9.17g already forbids reading the 0.72 vs 16.17 dispatcher comparison as 'D3 will be 20x slower' -- dispatch strategy and split count are different layers.
- [artifact .workbuddy/memory/2026-09-15.md (§D/§L, r4 production)] The r4 production configuration (hot pool + tensorops + MTP + adaptive gate) already runs at ~17 t/s. The submit-ahead probe reached 16.82 t/s with MTP OFF (its baseline is 9.16/9.45). Two different mechanisms land on the same throughput.

ALREADY RULED OUT (do not re-walk these):
- claim: Repairing the pool/slot content means the ~44% becomes available.
  why false: That repair is premise A and it moves nothing in the schedule: S1 keeps n_segs at 40 and the 39 (wait -> CPU -> submit) cycles remain. Correctness and throughput are bought by different changes, and only premise B touches n_segs.
- claim: Today's localization proves the pool contents are the defect.
  why false: It proves the ids and the lookup implementation are innocent, which is narrower. Two sub-suspects with different repairs remain: the table disagreeing with the leaf at consume time (a publication-ordering fix) and the slot contents themselves being wrong (a pool-fill fix). §9.18.6 exists precisely to separate them.
- claim: 16.82 t/s is D3's acceptance threshold.
  why false: It was measured with MTP off on a 9.16/9.45 baseline, while the production configuration with MTP on already runs ~17 t/s. Both are idle-time-filling mechanisms, so the factors are plausibly non-additive and the number has to be re-taken with MTP on.
- claim: D3 removes the race for free, so premise B does not matter for correctness.
  why false: Remove the segment boundary and there is indeed nothing left to interleave, but the slot_table is still host-written. If publication stays per-step the ordering requirement reappears between publish and consume; the race is relocated, not deleted.

Recorded the split into §9.18.7 of the remediation plan (S1 is a probe, not a defect; risk #1 promoted from precondition to mainline). Next measurements, in this order: (1) publish_slot_table call count per decode step -- cheap, host-side, and it decides whether premise B exists at all; (2) capture of ffn_moe_down-1's OUTPUT for both arms on graph 3, to separate 'the table disagrees with the leaf' from 'the slot contents are wrong'; (3) re-measure the submit-ahead ceiling with MTP ON before quoting any D3 acceptance number.

以下是引擎調校迴圈此刻的狀態。決定**下一個該做什麼**：一個具體的動作，
不要複述狀態。已經被排除的路線不要再走一次。

QUESTION: Is the segment-boundary ordering the cause of the S1 divergence, i.e. does turning the segmented async dispatcher off make the S1 arm bit-identical?

EVIDENCE ON HAND:
- [eng-20260915-213258-p25-gputime-noasync-r1] p25-gputime-noasync (CGC_SERVER_OA_ASYNC=0) gives md5 {dc055e63}, misses 13040, file_reads 36360 -- identical to the segmented anchor p25-gputime on all three.
    build=same-as-above  quotable=True
- [eng-20260915-213356-p25-slotgpu-noasync-r1] p25-slotgpu-noasync (CGC_SERVER_OA_ASYNC=0) gives md5 {29ca694a, 672585db, b8c705cc}, misses 14296, file_reads 39948 -- identical to the segmented S1 arm p25-slotgpu on all three. Two arms that are supposed to be switching a dispatcher produced the exact same digest SET and the exact same pool counters.
    build=same-as-above  quotable=False
- [artifact src/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp] Line 1745 gated the segmented dispatch on `getenv("CGC_OA_ASYNC") != nullptr && getenv("CGC_VERIFY_OP_TIMING") == nullptr && strcmp(ggml_backend_name(split_backend), "CPU") != 0`. A != nullptr test selects on PRESENCE, not value, so CGC_OA_ASYNC=0 -- and an empty string, since getenv returns "" and not NULL -- took the segmented branch. scripts/run_server.sh sets CGC_OA_ASYNC unconditionally from SERVER_OA_ASYNC, so there was no way to unset it through the runner either.

ALREADY RULED OUT (do not re-walk these):
- claim: CGC_SERVER_OA_ASYNC=0 selects the non-segmented dispatcher, so the earlier noasync pair isolates the ordering effect.
  why false: ggml-backend.cpp:1745 tested getenv("CGC_OA_ASYNC") != nullptr. The value is never read, so 0 selected the segmented branch exactly as 1 does, and the two arms reproduced the segmented arms' md5 sets and pool counters verbatim.

Re-run the pair against the rebuilt binary and compare within the pair only: p25-slotgpu-noasync bit-identical to p25-gputime-noasync means the ordering was the cause and the fix is to keep the segment drain tied to the hook rather than to the leaf; still different means the ordering is not it and the remaining suspect is the allocator layout (GGML_SCHED_DEBUG=2). Both arms must carry the same value of this switch or the comparison is meaningless -- the same class of mistake as A5's length rule, with a build switch instead of a generation length.

QUESTION: Rung 2 pushed the window to layers 18..19 by testing min_il = 2, 6, 10, 14, 18. Does that window name a bad LAYER, or does it only name the point where the number of served layers crosses a threshold?

EVIDENCE ON HAND:
- [eng-20260915-210801-p25-gputime-r1] Anchor: md5 {dc055e63}, stable over 3 rounds, generated 24 tokens, sample begins with the model's <think> reasoning preamble.
    build=same-as-above  quotable=True
- [eng-20260915-210508-p25-slotgpu-l20-r1] min_il=20, i.e. 20 served layers (20..39): md5 {dc055e63} -- same digest AND same 24-token length AND same sample prefix as the anchor.
    build=same-as-above  quotable=True
- [eng-20260915-211228-p25-slotgpu-l18-r1] min_il=18, i.e. 22 served layers: md5 {4991e6d2}, stable, generated only 6 tokens, sample is '巴黎是法国首都。' -- no <think> preamble and simplified rather than traditional Chinese, i.e. different from the anchor's very first character.
    build=same-as-above  quotable=True
- [eng-20260915-210953-p25-slotgpu-l6-r1] min_il=6, i.e. 34 served layers: md5 {7042e5e4}, stable, 12 tokens, sample is self-contradictory ('巴黎並非法國的首都，法國的首都是巴黎。').
    build=same-as-above  quotable=True
- [eng-20260915-210856-p25-slotgpu-l2-r1] min_il=2, i.e. 38 served layers: md5 {0d472bf5, 51548f50} over 3 rounds, UNSTABLE, 24 tokens, fluent but self-contradictory ('巴黎並非「法國的首都」，而是法國的首都。').
    build=same-as-above  quotable=False

ALREADY RULED OUT (do not re-walk these):
- claim: The divergence is caused by the pool-pressure hotspot at layer 2 (the pool counters report worst_layer=2, worst_distinct=248 against worst_slots=143).
  why false: min_il=18 serves layers 18..39 and diverges while NOT serving layer 2, so whatever breaks the answer at min_il=18 is not layer 2. Layer 2 is served only by the full arm and by min_il=2, and both of those already diverge for a reason the min_il=18 arm shares.
- claim: The extra nodes (table + CONT + GET_ROWS + VIEW, one set per served layer) move the answer by themselves, as soon as they exist.
  why false: min_il=39 (1 served layer), 38 (2) and 20 (20 layers, ~80 extra nodes) are each bit-identical to the baseline AND stable across rounds, with the same 24-token length. A node-presence effect would already show at one layer.

Run the p25-keepleaf control instead of a rung 3: with CGC_S1_KEEP_LEAF=1 every S1 node is built but mul_mat_id consumes the host leaf, so the post-sync readback walks all captured layers and prints gather-vs-leaf per layer (same=1/0). Mapping error -> some layer prints same=0 AND the arm stays bit-identical to the baseline. Threshold/global effect -> every layer prints same=1 AND the digest still differs, meaning the ids were never the problem. Deciding between the two by adding prefix arms is not possible; say so rather than quoting the {18,19} window as if it were the answer.

以下是引擎調校迴圈此刻的狀態。決定**下一個該做什麼**：一個具體的動作，
不要複述狀態。已經被排除的路線不要再走一次。

QUESTION: The keep-leaf readback exonerated the ids, but it was taken on a CONTROL arm where mul_mat_id consumes the host leaf. Is the id vector also correct in the REAL arm, where the gather is what mul_mat_id actually reads?

EVIDENCE ON HAND:

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
`git -C <main-worktree> rev-parse --git-path hooks`, run from a DIFFERENT cwd, returns `.git/hooks`. That value is not wrong, it is incomplete: it omits its base. Substituting it for a previously-absolute value (--absolute-git-dir) in check_build_tracked.sh --install-hook therefore looked like a one-line fix while actually relocating the write target to whatever the shell's cwd happened to be. In this repo the shell cwd is a linked worktree, where `.git` is a FILE, so `mkdir -p` / `cat >` / `chmod +x` all failed and the script still printed "installed pre-commit hook: <path>". Measured: `ls -ld <linked-worktree>/.git/hooks` -> "Not a directory". This is a strictly worse failure mode than the bug being fixed: the original wrote to a real directory that git does not read (recoverable by moving one file), whereas the naive fix writes nothing at all while reporting success (nothing to move).

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：
`HOOK_DIR="$(git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" rev-parse --git-path hooks)"` followed by `cat > "$HOOK_DIR/pre-commit"` -- the literal reading of the approved one-line change. From the main worktree the resolver returns the relative `.git/hooks`; from a linked worktree the shell cwd resolves it onto `<linked-worktree>/.git/hooks`, where `.git` is a regular file. mkdir/cat/chmod each fail, the script prints its success line, and exit code stays 0. Both the write target and the error are invisible.

它管轄的檔案：`scripts/check_build_tracked.sh`, `agent_harness/CONVENTIONS.md`

A path returned by a directory-resolving tool is expressed relative to THAT tool's working directory, not yours. Anchor every cross-directory path to your own base before using it. A relative return that is perfectly correct inside the tool's own cwd silently mis-targets everywhere else -- and the failure can be a total no-op that still prints success.

The per-capture design was chosen over the cheaper one-array-per-layer design while writing §9.18.7. The three MoE nodes of one layer (gate/up/down) are captured within microseconds of each other and would all have read the same shared array, so a fill landing between two of them -- drift inside a single layer inside a single pass -- would have printed identically on all three rows. 它管轄的檔案：`src/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-ops.cpp`, `Backup/compare_pool_row.py`

When an instrument snapshots a shared structure once per capture, store one copy per capture -- do not share one copy between captures that are being compared. A shared buffer makes the LAST capture's state the label for every earlier one, which silently deletes exactly the drift the captures were collected to expose, and it does so without any error: every row still prints a plausible value. The cost of per-capture storage is bounded and stateable (here: slot count x captures, arena grown on demand and capped with a printed warning when exhausted); the cost of a shared buffer is an unsupported conclusion. Corollary: if the snapshot cannot be taken (channel absent, arena full, key unparsable), write a distinct 'not annotated' token and make the reader treat it as absence of evidence -- never as an empty snapshot.

The dump's own volatility: `CGCENV LOG .../llama_server_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.log` carries a timestamp, and the `[preflight] free=NN%` / `[guard] ... free=NN%` lines track memory pressure. A launch configuration must be read by DUMPING it under the configuration you care about, not inferred from the default. Capture the resolved env as a normalised fingerprint so that 'the launch environment did not change' becomes a checkable claim -- and normalise correctly, or the instrument reports noise as change.

QUESTION: The keep-leaf control showed the extra nodes are inert. Does that leave the GPU-computed ids as the cause of the S1 divergence?

EVIDENCE ON HAND:
- [eng-20260915-212050-p25-keepleaf-dbg-r1] The post-sync readback compared the GPU gather against the host leaf for every captured layer, 6 samples per layer, all 39 layers. Split by token: TOKEN 0 agrees at EVERY layer (0 differences in 39 layers x 6 samples); rows >= 1 differ at EVERY layer (6/6 samples per layer). Example il=1: gather [2 105 7 9 5 106 1 84 | 0 103 0 74 121 110 3 99] vs leaf [2 105 7 9 5 106 1 84 | 8 0 50 4 20 6 55 3] -- identical for the first 8 entries, different for the next 8.
    build=same-as-above  quotable=True
- [eng-20260915-210508-p25-slotgpu-l20-r1] min_il=20: 20 served layers, hence 20 layers on which rows >= 1 differ, and the answer is still bit-identical to the baseline. The row>=1 difference is therefore provably benign.
    build=same-as-above  quotable=True
- [eng-20260915-211955-p25-keepleaf-r1] All 39 layers served with the leaf consumed: bit-identical to the baseline.
    build=same-as-above  quotable=True

ALREADY RULED OUT (do not re-walk these):
- claim: The GPU-computed ids differ from the host-written ids at some layer, so the mapping is wrong there.
  why false: The per-layer readback over 39 layers x 6 samples finds zero differences on token 0. The only differing rows are rows >= 1, uniformly at every layer, and min_il=20 carries 20 layers of that difference while staying bit-identical -- so those rows are padding, not a mapping error.

Measure the documented design instead of inventing one: CGC_S1_BUILD_LEAF=1 builds the leaf and leaves it unconsumed, which is exactly what llama-context.h's comment on cache_slot_table_tensors has always claimed S1 does ('the leaf itself is still built when this is on: it is simply not consumed ... a pure scheduler/dispatch change'). If p25-buildleaf is bit-identical, the fix is to make the implementation match its own documentation; if it is not, the suspect is the graph/allocator consequence of the missing node and the next instrument is the scheduler dump (GGML_SCHED_DEBUG=2) diffed between the real arm and the control.

以下是一條引擎調校迴圈裡「付過代價」的觀測。請把它一般化成**一條可重用的規訓**——
換一個問題也適用，而且讀者手上沒有這筆 episode 也必須能照著做。

觀測（because）：
The CGC-S1 post-sync readback prints a single `same=` bit for the whole id vector via memcmp. On every POST line it read same=0, which reads as 'the GPU gather disagrees with the host mapping at every layer, everywhere'. Split by token the picture is the opposite: token 0 agrees at all 39 layers across 6 samples each, and only rows >= 1 differ -- and those rows are padding whose difference is provably harmless (min_il=20 carries 20 layers of it and is bit-identical). The aggregate bit therefore supported the wrong conclusion and would have sent the investigation into the publish path for a defect that is not there. The general form: when the rows of a vector are not interchangeable (token 0 of a decode step vs a padding row, a real expert id vs a slot index), an aggregate equality test answers a question nobody asked.

它實際被違反的紀錄（counterexample_observed）：

它管轄的檔案：`src/llama.cpp/src/llama-context.cpp`

Do not let an aggregate comparison of a vector whose rows have different meanings stand in for the per-row comparison: one benign row's difference will read as total disagreement and hide the rows that agree.
